content.title: How To Watch Vanderbilt Commodores Men's Basketball
content.text: ✦ Edited and fact-checked by Sports Editor Taylor Kujawa, our resident TV expert with over eight years of covering sports. A look at the 2025–2026 Commodores Vanderbilt basketball is officially a national brand again, and the Memorial Magic has traveled all the way to Oklahoma City. Mark Byington has done a masterful job in his second season, pushing the Commodores to a school-record win total and their highest tournament seeding in over a decade. This isn’t the slow, methodical Vandy of the past; this is a high-octane unit that scores in bunches and thrives in the national spotlight. At the center of it all is Tyler Tanner, a sophomore who has played his way onto every All-American ballot in the country. Watching him navigate SEC defenses this year has been a treat, and I expect him to be one of the most talented players on the floor in most matchups this March. There’s a palpable sense of relief among the fanbase that Vanderbilt is finally acting like a basketball school again, and the expectations for a deep run are higher than they’ve been in a while. I’ve put this guide together to help you navigate the broadcast landscape so you don’t miss a second of this record-breaking season. Whether you’re a lifelong Vandy fan or a casual alum jumping on the bandwagon, here is how you can watch Vanderbilt basketball throughout the tournament. 2025–2026 Vanderbilt Commodores basketball TV schedule Vanderbilt kicks off its tournament run on Thursday, March 19, with a tricky matchup against McNeese State. As a #5 seed, the Dores have to be wary of the dreaded 12 vs. 5 upset, especially against a McNeese team with a history of giant-killing. This afternoon tip-off in Oklahoma City is a must-watch for anyone tracking the South Region bracket. prioritizes the Turner Sports networks. My top recommendation is Hulu + Live TV. It provides the most comprehensive coverage for the entire tournament, giving you truTV, TBS, and TNT, along with CBS for those crucial weekend games. It’s the most straightforward way to ensure you have every channel needed for a deep Vandy run. If you prefer a digital-only approach, the HBO Max app is an excellent secondary option. By upgrading to a Basic or Premium subscription, you can stream all the truTV, TBS, and TNT games live. This is particularly useful for the Round of 64, though you will still need a way to access CBS for later rounds. I’ve found that combining HBO Max with a basic antenna is a very cost-effective way to cover almost every tournament scenario. I strongly advise against using Fubo for the Commodores’ postseason. While Fubo is great for some sports, its lack of TNT Sports channels means you’ll be left in the dark for Vandy’s opening game and many subsequent matchups. Stick with a provider like Hulu + Live TV to keep the Tyler Tanner show on your screen. Find the best service in your area Enter your zip code below to see your area’s top TV providers. How to watch Vanderbilt basketball FAQ How can I watch Vanderbilt for free? You can watch Vanderbilt games for free by using an over-the-air antenna for matchups on CBS or by signing up for a free trial of a live TV streaming service like DIRECTV Stream. Some services offer temporary access that can get you through an entire weekend of games. How can I stream Vanderbilt without cable? To stream Vanderbilt without cable, I recommend subscribing to Hulu + Live TV or YouTube TV, as both carry truTV, TBS, TNT, and CBS. For the opening round specifically, you can also use the Max app with the B/R Sports Add-on. Can I watch Vanderbilt on truTV? Yes, you can watch Vanderbilt on truTV for their first-round matchup against McNeese State. Most major cable and satellite packages include truTV, as do streaming services like Hulu + Live TV and Sling TV. How can I watch Vanderbilt in March Madness? Vanderbilt’s March Madness games will air on a rotation of CBS, TBS, TNT, and truTV. You can follow the action on any device using the March Madness Live app, provided you have a login from a supported TV or streaming provider.
